title: When the Compass Falls
premise: Edmund Nakamura has spent a decade burying his father's legacy beneath careful anonymity, digging for other people's glory and keeping his name off every permit. When Vesper Kline, his father's old rival, buys the crew's contract and points them at the Meridian Range—the expedition that killed Edmund's father and was sworn off by everyone who survived it—Edmund must choose between walking away again and leading the climb before the season's first snows seal the passes. As the ascent strips away the crew's loyalties, Edmund discovers Kline never wanted the rumored shrine at all: she wants proof that Edmund's father falsified the find that made his reputation, evidence that would also clear the rival accusation that ruined her. In the ice caves above the tree line, Edmund finds his father's final field notes—honest, flawed, human—and must decide whether truth or myth is the better inheritance, choosing to publish both men's failures side by side as the snows close behind them.
about_author: Bram Quintana is a former trail-crew foreman who spent eleven seasons in the northern ranges before turning to fiction full-time. Their novels are known for terrain so precisely rendered readers check their own bootlaces.

chapters.title: The Long Way Around Names
chapters.summary: Edmund Nakamura, working under a borrowed surname on a salvage dig in the lowlands, is introduced through his meticulous hands and deliberate invisibility. A letter arrives from Vesper Kline offering a contract too large to refuse. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of being found.

chapters.title: Terms of the Sworn-Off
chapters.summary: The crew gathers at a roadhouse to hear Kline's terms: the Meridian Range, permits expiring in six weeks, a bonus none of them can refuse. Old-timer Ruth Alvarez recognizes the route and goes silent. Edmund agrees, telling himself it's just money. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: complicity disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: On the approach trek, the crew crosses country Edmund knows too well; he quietly reroutes them past the site of his father's last camp without explanation. Young cartographer Dev Okafor notices the detour and says nothing. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: grief expressed as navigation.

chapters.title: Kline's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vesper Kline's POV chapter: her decades-long grudge against Edmund's father, the ruin of her own career, and her private suspicion that the boy on her crew is more than he claims. She tests him with a detail only a Nakamura would know. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: ambition sharpened into obsession.

chapters.title: First Snowline
chapters.summary: The crew reaches base camp below the range as early snow dusts the high passes. Ruth confronts Edmund privately: she was on the original expedition and knows who he is. She gives him three days to tell the crew himself. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the cost of secrets compounding.

chapters.title: The Permit Clock
chapters.summary: A supply run reveals the concession office has flagged their paperwork—someone tipped off regulators. Kline accuses sabotage within the crew; trust fractures along old alliances. Dev defends Edmund without knowing why. POV: Dev. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by suspicion.

chapters.title: Ice Bridge
chapters.summary: The technical climb begins. A crevasse collapse nearly takes Dev; Edmund's improvised rescue saves him but exposes skills no hired hand should have. The crew starts asking questions Edmund can't deflect much longer. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: competence betraying concealment.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession
chapters.summary: Above the tree line, Ruth tells Edmund what really happened on the original expedition: his father sent the retreat party down and pushed on with two others, chasing the shrine. She's carried the guilt of surviving ever since. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: shared inheritance of blame.

chapters.title: Whiteout Protocol
chapters.summary: A storm pins the crew in tents for four days. Rations shrink, tempers fray, and Kline pushes to move early against every protocol. Edmund overrules her for the first time, openly asserting command. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: power shifting hands in the dark.

chapters.title: The Name in the Snow
chapters.summary: Dev discovers Edmund's real identity from an old expedition plaque cached at a waystation. He keeps the secret but begins watching him differently, hurt and awed. POV: Dev. Emotional beat: hero worship curdling into questions.

chapters.title: Halfway House
chapters.summary: At the mid-mountain depot, the crew finds evidence someone climbed ahead of them—fresh tracks, a cached cache with Kline's initials. She admits she sent a scout weeks ago. The crew realizes they were always instruments. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: betrayal recalibrating purpose.

chapters.title: Split Route
chapters.summary: With permits days from expiry, the crew votes: half descend with the injured, half push for the shrine site. Ruth stays; Dev stays; two walk out. Edmund leads the push, finally using his real name aloud. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: claiming identity as a burden willingly carried.

chapters.title: The Corridor of Falls
chapters.summary: The push team ascends a frozen waterfall corridor as meltwater refreezes behind them, cutting off retreat. Kline's scout is found alive but frostbitten, babbling about markings inside the ice. POV: Dev. Emotional beat: awe shading into fear of what's ahead.

chapters.title: Markings
chapters.summary: Inside the lower ice caves, they find survey marks—not ancient ones, but his father's. Edmund reads the handwriting like a voice. Kline watches him and understands, finally, who he is; she says nothing, which is its own confession. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: communion with the dead.

chapters.title: What Kline Wants
chapters.summary: Vesper lays it bare to Ruth: she believes Edmund's father fabricated the shrine discovery that destroyed her, and she needs the site itself to prove or disprove it. Her life's work balances on a verdict. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: obsession revealed as wound.

chapters.title: The Shrine Chamber
chapters.summary: They breach the chamber: the shrine is real, but small, human, altered—evidence his father documented it honestly, then exaggerated its scale under pressure from funders. Both truths coexist. Kline's certainty cracks. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: disillusionment as liberation.

chapters.title: Closing Weather
chapters.summary: The storm front arrives early. The exit corridor has iced shut; the only way down is the unclimbed east face. Kline freezes—literally and otherwise—and Edmund must take command of the woman who bought him. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: leadership stripped of ego.

chapters.title: East Face Descent
chapters.summary: The descent sequence: anchors, storms, a near-fatal slip that Kline catches Dev from, repaying nothing and everything. They lose the artifact crating but keep the field notes strapped to Edmund's chest. POV: Dev. Emotional beat: found family forged under load.

chapters.title: Below the Snows
chapters.summary: They reach the valley as the passes close behind them, sealed until spring. Frostbite claims two of Ruth's fingers; she calls it cheap rent. Kline sits apart, holding her disproven certainty. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: survival as quiet accounting.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: In the concession town, Kline offers Edmund co-authorship if he buries his father's exaggeration. He refuses the bargain and proposes instead a joint publication of both expeditions' complete records—her ruin and his father's flaw together. She walks out. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: integrity chosen over vindication.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: Months later, the joint paper publishes to controversy and, unexpectedly, respect. Edmund signs his own name to it. Dev joins his next crew; Ruth supervises; Kline sends a one-line note: 'The mountain kept better books than either of us.' POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: reconciliation without absolution.

chapters.title: When the Compass Falls
chapters.summary: Edmund returns alone to the base of the Meridian Range and buries his father's compass at the treeline—not a grave marker, but a handoff. The wilderness forgives nothing and forgets less, and he finally stops asking it to. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: homecoming to oneself.
